title: Patience
tomorrow: Pop's first steps since surgery. what do you say to a scared man?

cards: A waiting room. The TV on mute, the vending machine humming, a clock that only seems to move when nobody's looking. What does love do in a waiting room?
It waits. That's the first thing Paul says about love, in the King James words: “Charity suffereth long, and is kind.” Newer Bibles say love is patient.
But listen to the old phrase. Suffereth long. It even sounds slow, like that clock.

teach.b: In first Corinthians thirteen, Paul isn't describing a feeling.
Every item on his list is something love does or refuses to do: “Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up.” The list opens with waiting.

To suffer long is to stay with the slow thing, the person who takes ages to heal or to change, and not give up on them. And kind sits right beside it. Patience that has gone sour isn't what Paul means.
James adds a picture you can almost smell, rain on a dry field: “Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it.”
A farmer can't hurry the rain. He waits, and he keeps tending while he waits. So patience isn't doing nothing; it's staying faithful through a delay.
And Paul says God treats people this way too.
In Romans he writes of “the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering.” For Christians, patience with someone becomes a small copy of the patience they believe they've been shown.
So the line is short: love waits, with the field still tended, and the person still loved.

how: Christians describe patience as something grown over time, through prayer and everyday forbearance with others; 1 Corinthians 13 and James 5 are two passages they turn to.

o: love that waits through delay and stays kind
putting up with things without saying a word
a calm temper you're simply born with

games.q: how love waits — tap the pairs.

s: the KJV says 'charity suffereth long' where newer Bibles say 'love is patient'
same verse, older English: 'charity' for love, 'suffereth long' for patient.
in James, patience means doing nothing at all
the farmer waits for the rain and keeps tending the field.
in 1 Corinthians 13, patience is a calm feeling some people are born with
Paul's list is things love does: it suffers long, and is kind.

games.q: your little cousin is learning to tie his shoes, it's taking forever, and you're both going to be late. what would James's farmer do?
o: wait, and keep helping him, kindly, even though it's slow.
tie them yourself; patience doesn't mean being late.
sit back silently and let him struggle on his own.
games.why: the farmer waits for the rain and keeps tending. patience in James stays kind and stays involved.

practice: Find the slowest sound where you are: a fan, a fridge, traffic far off, rain if it's falling. Listen to it and let it set your pace; when the urge comes to check the time, notice it and come back to the sound.
If you pray, bring one slow-to-heal person to mind and hold them kindly.

wordCard.voice: Patience. Love that suffers long: waiting through delay, staying kind, still tending the field.

orig.note: Paul's verb in 1 Corinthians 13:4, which the KJV renders 'suffereth long.'

carryVoice: Hold on to this: love waits, and like a farmer, it keeps tending while it does. Day seventeen-forty, and counting.
